title: Slouchy cowl
subtitle: A wide, oversized cowl worked in the round with extra ease for drape.
excerpt: A wide cowl knitted in the round in stocking stitch on 6 mm needles with bulky-weight yarn, finishing at 90 cm circumference and 35 cm tall. The generous circumference means the cowl pools in soft folds at the neck when worn, rather than sitting close to the skin. A short rib at each opening keeps the edges flat.
sourceNotes: Oversized draped cowls in the round draw on the circular knitting techniques documented in Mary Thomas's Knitting Book (1938), citations only. The large-circumference cowl silhouette is a modern construction with no direct Victorian precedent.

glossaryTerms.definition: A circular needle with a fixed cord length. For a 90 cm circumference cowl, a 100 cm or 120 cm cord is the most comfortable; longer cords handle the stitch count without the stitches bunching.
A cast-on forming a neat elastic edge by using the tail and working yarn over two fingers simultaneously.

content.text: This is a wide cowl knitted in the round in stocking stitch on 6 mm needles with bulky-weight yarn, finishing at 90 cm circumference and 35 cm tall. The 90 cm circumference is about 30 cm wider than a fitted cowl, so the tube gathers into soft horizontal folds at the neck and shoulders when worn. A 1x1 rib at each opening prevents the edges from rolling back.

In-the-round construction was chosen because a stocking-stitch tube this wide would need a seam running up the full 35 cm height if worked flat, which would add bulk and sit visibly on the outside of the drape. A
fixed circular needle

at 100 cm or longer handles 126 stitches of bulky yarn most comfortably. The finished cowl needs about 300 m (approximately 300 g) of bulky-weight yarn. The generous circumference means the cowl pulled up over the chin rests comfortably over a coat.
What you need

items.name: Bulky-weight wool or wool-blend yarn
items.substitutions: Any bulky-weight yarn. A single-ply bulky gives the softest drape.

items.name: 6 mm circular needle, 100–120 cm (UK 4 / US 10)
items.substitutions: Magic loop on an 80 cm needle also works.

content.text: Gauge

14 sts x 18 rounds = 10 x 10 cm in stocking stitch in the round on 6 mm needles, blocked. One stitch per 10 cm off gauge shifts the finished circumference by approximately 6.4 cm at this stitch count: 15 sts per 10 cm gives about 84 cm circumference; 13 sts per 10 cm gives about 97 cm. The circumference shifts the drape character of the cowl significantly, so it is worth swatching before committing to 126 stitches.
Stitches used
K (knit): right needle from left to right through front of stitch, wrap yarn counterclockwise, draw loop through. In the round every body round is all knit for stocking stitch.
P (purl): used in the rib sections only.
Pattern
Cast on
Use the
long-tail cast-on

to place 126 stitches on the needle. Before beginning, calculate the tail: tail_cm = (needle circumference mm x stitch count) / 10 + 15. For 6 mm needles (circumference approximately 18.8 mm) and 126 stitches: (18.8 x 126) / 10 + 15 = 236.9 + 15 = about 252 cm. Leave a tail of at least 252 cm; wind it around a small card before making the slip knot.
Stitch count check-in: after the cast-on you should have 126 stitches on the needle. Join to work in the round without twisting. Place a stitch marker.
Body
Rib section (5 rounds): *K1, P1; repeat from * to end. (126 sts)
Body (63 rounds): K all stitches every round. (126 sts)
Work the body until the cowl measures 33 cm from the cast-on edge. At the halfway mark (approximately round 32 of the 63 body rounds), count your stitches.
Stitch count check-in: at round 32 of the body you should have 126 stitches on the needle.
Closing rib section (5 rounds): *K1, P1; repeat from * to end. (126 sts)
Bind off
Stretchy bind-off
in rib pattern. A standard bind-off on 126 stitches of bulky yarn with no stretch will produce an obviously narrower top opening that resists pulling over the head.
Common faults

Twisted join. With 126 stitches of bulky yarn the cast-on tail is long and the join is harder to check. Lay the full cast-on edge flat on a table before joining the first round, confirming the stitches all face the same direction.

Cowl too stiff to drape softly. If the cowl looks like a rigid tube rather than a soft loop, the gauge is too tight. Bulky yarn on 6 mm should give a relaxed, drapey fabric. Try 7 mm needles for the swatch if this happens.
Cowl too short to gather at the neck. The 35 cm height is chosen so the cowl drapes with at least 5 to 8 cm of horizontal folds when worn. If in doubt, knit 5 cm more before binding off.
Finishing
Weave in both tails at the cast-on join and bind-off. Block by wetting and laying flat or draping over a round form to dry in the round shape.
Care
Handwash in cool water with wool wash. Lay flat or over a round form to dry. Do not hang while wet as the weight will stretch the tube.
What to try next

The infinity cowl is a narrower, longer tube that is worn doubled. The basic cowl is the same construction at a closer-fitting circumference. The ribbed cowl replaces the stocking-stitch body with 2x2 rib for a stretchier version.
